rationale:
AMENDED 2026-11-12 (CHANGELOG.md): the owner's strategic mix is the default and the yardstick; VWRA is the world sleeve's designated line and the exposure view's neutral zero point (world = 50). This is the latest set of 100 pillars. It is the round-3 candidate, revised to fix every blocking problem and apply the fixes from the five round-3 audits (portfolio 25, quant 23, execution 25, data 27, skeptic 25).

What the system does with the owner's money:
- Each month, 2,500 AED becomes US$678.74 (2,500 / 3.6725 = US$680.74, minus the US$2 FX minimum). VWRA is the yardstick every option is measured against, not the only answer.
- Sleeves: core world (VWRA), S&P 500 (SPXS, VUAA, CSPX), Nasdaq-100 (XNAS, CNDX, EQQU), developed ex-US (EXUS), emerging markets (EIMI), factor and small-cap (IWVL, IWQU, WSML), gold (IGLN) and bonds.
- By default every deposit goes to VWRA. No score-driven or owner-policy rule has yet beaten holding the world after costs under both execution timings. Rotation lost, sending each deposit to the top-ranked fund was a coin flip, and selling on trend cost 1-3 points a year.
- Owner policy weights (policy_targets) now route money only if REC07, run exactly as the live rule would at US$681 a month, beats the world in every period under both timings. The round-3 auditors found that the CHANGELOG-override route broke GOAL.md's evidence rule, so it has been removed. Amending GOAL.md is the owner's decision, not something the system offers.

How the 100 pillars are organised. There are three separate views and no mixed composite:
- Line view: which UCITS line to buy within a sleeve (cost, tracking, tax-rule fragility, durability, fund events). CST10 picks the line.
- Exposure score X: whether an equity sleeve deserves a tilt, scored against VWRA = 50. It holds only pillars that REC04 can rebuild point-in-time: currency value, 5-year reversal, four factor loadings on one common factor set, a merged drawdown pillar, downside asymmetry and tail fatness.
- Fit view: what a purchase does to the owner's real holdings. It now uses one beta everywhere, so the fit check is exactly 0 when tilts are 0.

Everything else is a gate, a hard constraint, context or a record kept for testing. Any pillar whose source is unverified has weight 0.

Main round-3 fixes:
- One beta definition (FAC05: a univariate 120-month Ledoit-Wolf beta on the single world reference). It feeds EXR02, FIT04, RSK01 and RSK04, so 'FIT04 = 0 when tilts are 0' now holds identically.
- One common Ken French factor set (Developed 5 factors plus Developed momentum) for every equity sleeve and VWRA. CMA is orthogonalised to HML so that value is not counted twice.
- The REC04 gate now tests active returns against the world (a deflated information ratio). The existing gate used each strategy's absolute Sharpe and could never pass. N_TRIALS now counts the audit rounds.
- Data sources now have fallbacks: BIS is the primary REER source (Taiwan and Korea added), with ECB, BoE and cached-value fallbacks when FRED is down, and a cached Shiller link. Status labels are corrected where the snapshot store does not exist, where the Vanguard 'NAV at closure' label is gone, and where MAC02's short OAS history cannot support a 20-year percentile.

The pillars are not yet proven to be the best 100. Three tests will settle that: the REC03 redundancy check on the point-in-time panel, the REC04 exact-rule backtest with a holdout, and 36 months of live record.

families.name: Eligibility, line integrity and data quality
families.purpose: Pass/fail gates and data checks on the exact LSE line: domicile and the physical-ETC branch, USD quote, product complexity, asset class, freshness, price integrity, proxy mapping and splice, IBKR orderability, coverage and source reconciliation. Gates decide what may receive money and are never averaged into a score. The core's designated line (VWRA) is never blocked by an owner-input or coverage gate.

families.name: Implementation cost on the UCITS line
families.purpose: Line view (the line score sums to 100 within each sleeve: CST 53, TAX 21, DUR 19, line EVT 7). Covers known-sign drags on the line actually bought, compared with other lines in the same sleeve: TER (CST01), tracking beyond TER (CST02), its stability, price noise, traded value and residue. CST10 is the single line-choice formula. It fails closed when TER history is incomplete.

families.name: Withholding, tax-rule fragility and distribution drag
families.purpose: Line view. Look-through US withholding is used only where 3 years of CST02 are missing. Also scores the fragility of a cost advantage beyond TER that rests on one tax rule, and distribution friction. When TAX01 is inactive by design, TAX03 and TAX05 are renormalised to 2/3 and 1/3; this is not treated as missing data.

families.name: Fund durability and switch readiness
families.purpose: Line view. The chance the line survives 15 years without a forced switch: size, age and ready substitutes are scored. Physical-ETC custody is a gate. Flows, issuer record, counterparty exposure and benchmark history are recorded once the weekly snapshot store exists (not yet started). Feeds the structural sell rules.

families.name: Long-horizon expected return
families.purpose: Exposure view X (EXR 20, FAC 40, RSK 40 = 100; VWRA = 50). Scored on each equity sleeve's reference index, never on its best line. Only currency value (EXR06) and 5-year reversal (EXR08) are scored. Together with FAC01 they sit under a value-cluster cap of 25% of X (24.8% now). EXR02 turns scored pillars into a beta-consistent expected excess return, using the single FAC05 beta, for FIT04. Its b_j coefficients are labelled unestimated priors everywhere they appear.

families.name: Rewarded factor exposure
families.purpose: Exposure view. Value, profitability, investment (orthogonalised to value) and quality-conditioned size loadings, from point-in-time regressions of every equity sleeve and VWRA on one common factor set (Ken French Developed 5 factors plus Developed momentum) with a release lag. Loadings are shrunk by their t-statistics and scored relative to VWRA's. FAC05 holds the single market beta, from its own univariate regression on the world reference.

families.name: Holdability (one-sided against VWRA)
families.purpose: Exposure view. Every scored RSK pillar is one-sided: worse than VWRA is penalised and calmer earns nothing above 50. RSK01 merges the drawdown path. Its maximum-drawdown and time-under-water parts are raw, because holdability is about the actual loss. Its stress-window part is beta-adjusted with the FAC05 beta. RSK03 is downside asymmetry and RSK05 tail fatness. Stress windows enter only after they have ended.

families.name: Fund-level exposure hazards
families.purpose: Not in X. CON04 (restricted markets) and CON05 (thematic hype) are line-level gates. Breadth, country/currency mix and sector concentration are context, and their portfolio limits sit in FIT.

families.name: Fit with the current portfolio (state-dependent)
families.purpose: Fit view: its own 100 points, with the current portfolio = 50. For equity sleeves it combines expected alpha (40%, using one beta: beta_i,P = beta_i,world / beta_P,world), down-market correlation, diversification return and ex-ante tracking error against VWRA. For gold and bond sleeves FIT04 is context. Sleeve gap and months-to-cure drive routing and sells. Limits on US weight, sectors, single names and line count are hard constraints with weight 0. Until owner positions exist, the portfolio is taken as 100% core.

families.name: Trend (record only)
families.purpose: 12-1 and residual momentum are recorded and tested in REC04 as a pre-registered variant. The crash state, core trend flag and relative-performance display are information only. Trend is never a reason to sell.

families.name: News and structural events (agents)
families.purpose: Ten agents with cited, dated sources. Line events (EVT01, EVT02, EVT05) are penalty-only in the line score and gate deposits at severity 2 or more. Code-computable triggers, such as EVT02's cheaper-substitute test, are computed by code; agents only confirm facts. EVT07 severity 3 is a hard gate. EVT10 numbers are accepted only after code confirms the quoted text.

families.name: Live record and rule testing
families.purpose: Judges the system on the owner's money and decides when anything may start moving money. It covers money-weighted return against a VWRA-only shadow, point-in-time snapshots, the redundancy matrix and live IC, and the exact-rule backtest gate (REC04, a deflated information ratio on active returns against the world). It also keeps the funding and execution log, behaviour and attribution, and the exact-routing owner-policy test at US$681 a month (REC07).

families.name: Macro context
families.purpose: Context for the weekly note, the drawdown protocol, order-time caution and the owner's choice of diversifier share D. Weight 0, because macro predictors fail out of sample (Welch and Goyal 2008). Every FRED input has an ECB, BoE or BIS fallback plus a cached last-good value with an age flag.

pillars.name: Irish or Luxembourg UCITS domicile, non-US-situs, with a physical-ETC branch (gate)
pillars.definition: Pass branch (a): the ISIN starts with IE or LU, the fund is UCITS and it is not US-situs (IE is preferred over LU on the same index; the cost shows in TAX01). Pass branch (b), for the gold or silver sleeve only: an IE-issued, physically backed precious-metal ETC holding allocated, segregated LBMA bullion in a non-US vault with a named custodian, confirmed by DUR02. US-domiciled or US-listed funds fail; they can be watched but never bought. A held line turning from pass to fail triggers S1.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv ISIN and scope columns; iShares UK product page domicile and UCITS fields; DUR02 for branch (b)
pillars.evidence: GOAL.md: US-listed funds cost 30% dividend withholding and carry US estate-tax exposure above US$60,000. The Ireland-US treaty gives Irish funds 15%. IGLN.L is an Irish ETC note, not a UCITS fund, hence branch (b).

pillars.name: USD LSE line and price-unit check (gate)
pillars.definition: Pass if the line trades on the LSE in USD (yfinance currency == USD). GBp, GBP and EUR lines are mapped to their USD sibling by ISIN (SSAC.L to ISAC.L, SPXP.L to SPXS.L). A non-USD line is eligible only if the sleeve has no affordable eligible USD line, and its FX cost is then charged in CST10. Flags 100x GBp/GBP jumps.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L currency; universe_ucits_*.csv currency and ISIN columns
pillars.evidence: SPXS.L closes at US$14.95 (USD) while SPXP.L closes at 1118.6 GBp. Naive GBp-vs-USD comparisons produced fake 292-342 bp gaps.

pillars.name: Product-complexity gate
pillars.definition: Fails leveraged, inverse, daily-reset, option-overlay (covered-call, buffer) and single-stock products, identified from fund name, universe scope and issuer structure fields.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv name and scope; iShares structure fields; justETF profile replication field
pillars.evidence: Daily-reset funds decay with volatility (Cheng and Madhavan 2009). Covered calls give up upside (Israelov and Nielsen 2015).

pillars.name: Asset-class and sleeve eligibility (gate)
pillars.definition: Maps each line to one sleeve. Equity UCITS lines go to the core or an equity satellite. Physical gold ETCs passing ELG01(b) go to the gold sleeve only. Investment-grade government or aggregate bond funds with a duration of 5 years or more go to the diversifier sleeve only. Gold and bond sleeves are owner-sized and never score-targeted. Money-market, T-bill, 0-1 year, ultra-short, overnight-swap and multi-asset funds always fail. Lines with no pre-registered sleeve (XDEW, R2US, CUSS) are scored weekly but cannot receive deposits.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv scope column (XDEW correction and duplicate removal pending; see allocation step 1); issuer asset-class and duration fields
pillars.evidence: PILLAR_AUDIT: the old composite correlated -0.77 with 1-year volatility and put 7 T-bill or bond funds in its top 20. This gate keeps cash out by construction.

pillars.name: Feed freshness
pillars.definition: LSE trading days since the last print with volume above 0 on the USD line. More than 5 days: not buyable. More than 7 days on a held line: structural review under S1, confirmed with an issuer or Investegate notice.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L daily close and volume
pillars.evidence: DECISION_RULES rule 1 treats a core feed stale for more than 7 days as structural. SPYY.L showed about 5% zero-volume sessions.

pillars.name: Price integrity
pillars.definition: Count over 252 sessions of daily .L returns beyond 6 robust sigmas that the sleeve reference line does not match on the same or next day (same sign, at least half the size), plus unit jumps and runs of repeated closes. Any unmatched event suspends the line's price-based pillars until it is explained.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and reference-line daily closes
pillars.evidence: The audit traced fake readings to a stale Yahoo NAV and unit mix-ups. CNDX.L printed the same close on 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06.

pillars.name: Proxy mapping, approved equivalents and splice fidelity
pillars.data_source: iShares UK 'Benchmark Index' field; justETF profiles; yfinance monthly closes, including ^NDX (verified 2026-11-07: 1985-10 to 2026-11, 494 rows); iShares holdings CSV (SSAC productId 251850 verified: 1,738 rows, US 63.88%; SWDA verified); Ken French Developed, Developed ex US and Emerging files (verified to 2026-09)
pillars.evidence: Audit mapping errors included USMV/ACWV to MVOL, VTI to CSPX and IOO to VWRA. Vanguard publishes only the top 10 holdings for VWRA. Round 3 (quant): without a pre-QQQ splice, the Nasdaq-100 2000-02 drawdown was invisible in the 2003-2014 holdout, and the region mix had no as-of date, a possible look-ahead.

pillars.name: IBKR orderability
pillars.definition: An owner-confirmed flag: orderable: {LINE: {ok, checked_on, ibkr_product_class, complex_permission_needed}}. It is renewed every 100 days and whenever a line first enters the shortlist; if expired or absent, the line fails. The core's designated line VWRA.L is seeded as orderable from the owner's existing holding and is never blocked. Entries for the core fallbacks FWRA.L and ACWD.L must be checked by the owner before either can receive money; until then the core fallback chain is VWRA only. For ETCs (IGLN) the owner also records IBKR's product classification. If no line in the target sleeve passes, the deposit routes to the next sleeve, then to the core.
pillars.data_source: Owner check in TWS or the IBKR client portal, stored in config/portfolio.yaml. The orderable block is not yet in the file (data tests 1 and 16) and must be added, seeded with VWRA.L, before the first monthly run.
pillars.evidence: Retail access to UCITS lines depends on the IBKR entity and KID availability, and IBKR has no API reachable from the cloud. Round 3 (execution): the earlier fallback chain FWRA then ACWD skipped this gate.

pillars.name: Coverage and source freshness
pillars.definition: The share of the line's scored pillar weight, counting only pillars with verified sources, that has a live reading this week. Age limits: holdings 35 days (45 for month-end publishers such as Vanguard), tracking difference 100 days, TER 120 days, cached FRED or Shiller values 45 days. Below 70% the line cannot receive money, except VWRA, which is exempt. Coverage is shown next to every score.
pillars.data_source: Engine pillar table and 'as of' dates
pillars.evidence: PILLAR_AUDIT: filling missing values with 50 hid 14-23% gaps. The Vanguard holdings page was 38 days old on the test date.

pillars.name: Cross-source reconciliation
pillars.definition: Compares issuer, Yahoo and justETF figures for TER (2 bps tolerance) and date-matched NAV (20 bps). AUM is compared like with like (fund level, in USD at the same date's FX, same as-of date) with a 10% tolerance, and only below DUR01's US$5bn saturation; above it the AUM check is skipped, because it cannot change DUR01. Holdings stand-ins are compared on region weights against the issuer's own figures, with a 2-point tolerance (for example SSAC US 63.88% against VWRA's Vanguard month-end US 62.24%). The Vanguard region table is read by a pinned parser. If the table is absent, the reconciliation reads missing and the stand-in is flagged unreconciled, which is not a pass: FIT08 then fails open for the core and closed for satellites. Stand-in sector weights are cross-checked against yfinance VT sector weightings. A breach blocks the affected pillar until resolved, and the source used is logged.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK product pages and holdings CSV; vanguard.co.uk month-end region table (pinned parser to build); justETF profiles; yfinance .L info and VT funds_data; universe_ucits_*.csv
pillars.evidence: Found: the universe lists VWRA TER 0.19% against 0.14% (fix pending); justETF shows VWRA EUR 56.3bn and yfinance US$87.3bn, which would have tripped a naive 10% AUM check. The Vanguard region source returned region weights in one data test and only top-10 ISO codes in a later one.

pillars.name: TER of the share class
pillars.definition: Ongoing charge of the exact USD share class in bps a year, scored against the sleeve's median eligible line with k = 10 bps. Every change is appended to ter_history (date, TER, source URL), which is seeded from the issuers' annual-report PDFs back to the start of each CST02 window. Any rise opens a review (EVT02, S2). The universe VWRA TER is corrected to 0.14 before any CST run.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK product page TER; justETF profile TER (e.g. VWRA 0.14%); issuer annual-report PDFs for ter_history (download verified); issuer KIDs confirmed by EVT02; reconciled by ELG10
pillars.evidence: Fees are the one certain drag (Sharpe 1991) and the most reliable predictor of fund outcomes (Kinnel 2016). A 0.15-point gap compounds to about 2.2% of terminal wealth over 15 years.

pillars.name: Tracking beyond TER, relative to the sleeve reference line (fails closed)
pillars.definition:
First compute G_i, the annualised gap between line i's USD LSE total return and the same-index reference line's over at least 3 years (5 where available), using 20-day average prices at both ends. Restate it at current TERs: G_i = gap_raw_i + (TERbar_i - TERnow_i) - (TERbar_ref - TERnow_ref), where TERbar is the time-weighted TER actually charged, from ter_history.
Then CST02_i = G_i + (TERnow_i - TERnow_ref): the tracking edge beyond TER, so that TER itself is scored only in CST01. It is shrunk toward 0 by its standard error.
Fails closed: CST02 is missing for the whole sleeve unless ter_history has a dated, sourced seed entry for every line in the sleeve covering the whole window. Lines on different indices are never compared.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L daily closes (verified for all issuers); ter_history seeded from annual reports (CST01); iShares UK performance tables for the reference line's absolute tracking difference | STATUS: verified for iShares-only sleeves; unverified and fails closed for Vanguard, Invesco and Xtrackers lines until ter_history is seeded from another source (justETF snapshots from now on, or annual reports via the Central Bank of Ireland register)
pillars.evidence: Tracking difference persists by fund (Elton, Gruber, Comer and Li 2002). Raw 3-year gaps measured 2026-11-07: SPXS vs CSPX +19.3 bps a year (+17.3 beyond the 2 bp TER difference), VUAA vs CSPX -0.1, XNAS vs CNDX +16.8, EQQU vs CNDX +4.2. Round 3 (data): a TER change missing from ter_history would silently bias G, hence fail-closed.

pillars.name: Tracking-difference stability
pillars.definition: Standard deviation of the last 5 calendar-year gaps against the sleeve reference line, each restated at current TERs (iShares lines: calendar-year tracking difference from the issuer table), in bps, with k = 15 bps.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L closes; iShares UK calendar-year performance table; CST01 ter_history
pillars.evidence: An erratic yearly gap signals sampling, lending swings or one-off reclaims that may not repeat. Its redundancy with CST04 is tested before launch in REC03.

pillars.name: Price noise against the sleeve reference line
pillars.definition: Annualised standard deviation of daily return differences against the sleeve reference line over 1 year, in bps.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L daily closes
pillars.evidence: Measured: CSPX vs VUAA 68 bps, CSPX vs SPXS 72 bps, VWRA vs FWRA 218 bps. More noise means a larger random premium paid on each buy (Frino and Gallagher 2001).

pillars.name: Quoted bid-ask spread (record until verified)
pillars.definition: A weekday job takes one snapshot at 14:00 London, Tuesday to Thursday. A quote is kept only if regularMarketTime is within 25 minutes, bid < ask, both sizes are above 0, the currency is USD and the spread is under 200 bps. The pillar is the 20-snapshot median in bps. Weight 0 until 20 valid snapshots exist.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L bid, ask and regularMarketTime
pillars.evidence: Data test 2: weekend quotes were stale or crossed (CSPX bid 841.29 above ask 799.20), and Yahoo LSE quotes are delayed.

pillars.name: LSE traded value and zero-volume days
pillars.definition: Log of the 63-session median daily traded value on the USD line (close x volume, US$), saturating at US$5m a day, minus a penalty for the share of zero-volume sessions (0% none, 20% or more maximum). Also sets the S1/S2 switch-size rule.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L daily volume and close
pillars.evidence: Liquidity goes with tighter spreads and smaller premiums (Petajisto 2017). Medians: CSPX about US$107-158m a day, VWRA about US$40m, FWRA about US$3.6m. Its redundancy with DUR01 is tested in REC03; the two are merged if |rho| is 0.85 or more.

pillars.name: Premium or discount to NAV, time-aligned (record)
pillars.definition: Mean |aligned price / NAV - 1| over 20 sessions, in bps, where aligned price = LSE close(t) adjusted by the reference index or futures move between the NAV valuation point and 16:30 London. iShares lines use the daily Historical NAVs sheet. VWRA has only the vanguard.co.uk embedded navPrices JSON spot value (no history), so it has no 20-session value. Weight 0, because the main non-iShares buy lines (VWRA, VUAA, SPXS, XNAS) have no daily NAV history. Yahoo navPrice is never used. The same aligned method is used for the S1 discount check.
pillars.data_source: iShares fund-document API 'Historical NAVs' sheet (verified: CSPX daily NAV 2010-05 to 2026-11-06); vanguard.co.uk embedded navPrices JSON (verified spot: USD 183.4672 on 2026-11-06, no history); other issuers unverified
pillars.evidence: A naive close/NAV gap is about +0.75% from timing alone (CSPX 802.21 against NAV 796.22). The vanguard.co.uk 'NAV at closure' label no longer exists (data test 3).

pillars.name: Whole-share residue at deposit size
pillars.definition: Expected uninvested share of a whole-share order, averaged over orders of US$340-760: (order - commission - floor((order - commission) / price) x price) / order. A line priced above 0.9 x US$679 is flagged as not buyable in one month. Weight 0.05 in the line score, because residue is carried into next month and its money cost is priced in CST10. Fractional shares are assumed unavailable until EVT08 confirms otherwise.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L USD price; deposit size from config/portfolio.yaml
pillars.evidence: Prices on 2026-11-07: CSPX US$802.21 and CNDX US$1,562.80, both above one deposit; SPXS US$14.95, XNAS US$63.16, VUAA US$143.90, EQQU US$665.13, EXUS US$44.75, EIMI US$48.91.

pillars.name: Realised execution cost from owner fills
pillars.definition: Median over the line's last 6 owner fills of (fill - mid at order entry) / mid plus commission / order, in bps, with each fill tagged by its execution-ladder rung (allocation 3(g)). Missing below 3 fills; from 3 fills it takes 0.10 of CST weight from CST06.
pillars.data_source: IBKR activity statement CSV in inputs/ibkr/ (folder and parser not yet created); fills block in config/portfolio.yaml (to be added)
pillars.evidence: Measures the owner's real order type, size and time, where free estimators fail (CST05). Data tests 3 and 4: no statements, folder or parser exist yet.

pillars.name: 15-year all-in cost per deposited dollar (line choice)
pillars.definition:
Expected annual cost in bps:
CST10_i = -(TD_ref + G_i) + 0.5 x TAX03_i + amortised entry costs + FX cost for a non-USD line.
- TD_ref is the reference line's absolute tracking difference against the net index (iShares table; positive means it beat the index). Where it is unavailable it is set to 0; it is common to every line in the sleeve, so the ranking is unchanged.
- G_i is CST02's TER-restated raw gap, so the TER currently charged is included exactly once.
- TAX03 is now the tax-rule-dependent advantage beyond TER.
- Entry costs are spread over 15 years: the commission share, half the spread where CST05 or CST09 exist, and residue x r_forgone. r_forgone = 0.6% a month, the expected nominal equity return given up while money waits; it is one constant in pillar_scales.yaml, shared with allocation 3(a).
If CST02 is missing for the sleeve (fail-closed), every candidate uses TERnow + TAX01 instead. Weight 0; it ranks lines inside a sleeve. A unit test reproduces the worked figures below.
pillars.data_source: Derived from CST01, CST02, CST05, CST08, CST09, TAX01, TAX03; IBKR commission US$1.70 minimum and FX US$2 minimum | STATUS: verified for iShares-only sleeves; unverified and fails closed for Vanguard, Invesco and Xtrackers lines until ter_history is seeded from another source (justETF snapshots from now on, or annual reports via the Central Bank of Ireland register)
pillars.evidence: Worked figures: SPXS = -(17 + 19.3) + 0.5 x 17.3 = -27.65 bps plus entry costs; VUAA = -(17 - 0.1) + 0 = -16.9 bps plus entry costs. SPXS is about 10.75 bps a year cheaper after the tax-rule haircut. Round 3 (portfolio): the haircut is now based on the gap beyond TER.

pillars.name: US dividend withholding drag
pillars.definition: Look-through US weight x US dividend yield x fund-level rate (Irish physical 15%, Irish swap on a qualified index about 0%, Luxembourg physical 30%), in bps a year. The US yield is the sum of the proxy's dividends with ex-dates in the 12 months ending today (not ending at the last payment). Scored only when CST02 is missing for the sleeve; otherwise it is inactive by design and TAX03/TAX05 are renormalised.
pillars.data_source: iShares holdings CSV Location column (latest-holdings.csv by productId); vanguard.co.uk month-end region weights for Vanguard lines; yfinance Ticker.dividends of the US proxy, window anchored to today
pillars.evidence: Ireland-US treaty rate 15%. About 1.3% yield x 15% = about 20 bps, matching the measured SPXS-over-CSPX gap. Data test 5: the anchor matters (EWJ 4.04% anchored to today vs 4.71% anchored to the last payment).

pillars.name: Non-US level-1 withholding drag (record)
pillars.definition: Sum over countries of fund weight x country dividend yield (12 months ending today) x unrecoverable rate for an Irish or Luxembourg fund, in bps a year. Weight 0 until the treaty table is verified; CST02 captures the realised effect meanwhile.
pillars.data_source: Holdings Location weights (verified); country yields from EWJ, EWU, EWG, MCHI and INDA dividends, window anchored to today (verified; INDA flagged, no dividend in 23 months); treaty-rate table kept by hand (unverified)
pillars.evidence: Gross-to-net index gaps are 10-30 bps for ex-US and EM. The hand-kept table has no verified source.

pillars.name: Tax-rule dependence of a cost advantage (beyond TER)
pillars.definition: The part of a line's cost advantage beyond TER (its CST02 relative to the physical same-index peer) that depends on one tax rule (for example section 871(m) for swap S&P 500 lines), in bps. One-sided: 0 bps scores 50, falling to the floor at 25 bps or more. Half of it is charged in CST10.
pillars.data_source: Derived from replication type (justETF profile: SPXS 'Synthetic (Unfunded swap)') and CST02; rule status watched by EVT06 | STATUS: verified for iShares-only sleeves; unverified and fails closed for Vanguard, Invesco and Xtrackers lines until ter_history is seeded from another source (justETF snapshots from now on, or annual reports via the Central Bank of Ireland register)
pillars.evidence: SPXS vs CSPX: 19.3 bps raw gap, of which about 2 bps is the TER difference, so 17.3 bps depends on the swap tax treatment and would vanish if the rule changed. Round 3 (portfolio) fix.

pillars.name: Bond-interest withholding (diversifier sleeve, record)
pillars.definition: Share of a bond fund's income not exempt for an Irish fund x rate x yield, in bps a year. Weight 0 until the rules table is verified.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK bond holdings CSV Location column (verified); rules table kept by hand (unverified)
pillars.evidence: The US portfolio-interest exemption (IRC 871(h), 881(c)) frees most US bond interest.

pillars.name: Distribution friction
pillars.definition: 0 for an accumulating class. For a distributing class (for example EQQU): the cost of reinvesting each payment (US$1.70 per payment) or its cash drag at r_forgone, in bps a year. A distributing class is eligible only where its sleeve has no affordable accumulating USD line.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv accumulating column; yield from the proxy's 12-month dividends ending today
pillars.evidence: Irish funds pay non-residents without Irish withholding and the UAE has no income tax, so only the reinvestment commission and idle cash differ.

pillars.name: Fund and share-class size
pillars.definition: min(fund AUM, 5 x share-class AUM) where the share-class AUM is known, otherwise fund AUM, in US$ at the same date's FX, log-scaled from US$50m and saturating at US$5bn.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK net assets of fund and of share class; justETF fund size converted to USD (e.g. VWRA EUR 56.3bn); yfinance totalAssets (VUAA US$89.0bn, EXUS US$8.2bn); reconciled by ELG10 below US$5bn only
pillars.evidence: European ETF closures concentrate in funds under about US$100m. Its redundancy with CST06 is tested in REC03.

pillars.name: Physical-ETC structure and custody (gold sleeve gate)
pillars.definition: For ELG01 branch (b): allocated and segregated LBMA good-delivery metal, a named custodian with a vault outside the US, an independent trustee or security over the metal, and no unsecured counterparty beyond settlement. Pass or fail, from the product page or base prospectus, or an owner check with a date in etc_checks. Re-checked yearly and on any EVT05 custodian event. Weight 0 (gate).
pillars.data_source: iShares Physical Gold ETC page (verified: 289.74 tonnes, TER 0.12%, bar-list link) and base prospectus PDF (verified download); Invesco pages (HTTP 406, blocked); owner check
pillars.evidence: An ETC is a debt note of a special-purpose issuer. Kept unverified until the prospectus custody terms are parsed and the owner's etc_checks entry exists.

pillars.name: Net flows, 12 months (one-sided, record until history exists)
pillars.definition: (Shares outstanding now - 12 months ago) x NAV / AUM 12 months ago, in %. Outflows are penalised and inflows are neutral. Missing until 52 weekly snapshots exist, counted from the first real snapshot written by the snapshot job (not yet started). The signed series is logged for REC03.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK shares outstanding (current value verified: CSPX 188,328,592 on 06/Nov/2026). Weekly snapshot store not started (data test 8); the snapshot writer is in the files to create. For others, justETF size change minus price return (unverified, noisy).
pillars.better_when: higher up to 0 (outflows bad, inflows neutral)
pillars.evidence: Outflows come before closures. Inflows are not rewarded, because flows chase returns (Dannhauser and Pontiff 2019). Round 3: the earlier 'snapshotted weekly from 2026-W45 (verified)' label was false and has been corrected.

pillars.name: Share-class age
pillars.definition: Years since the USD line launched, saturating at 5. The universe or issuer first date is preferred over yfinance fundInceptionDate.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv first_date; iShares inception date; justETF profile inception
pillars.evidence: Closure risk is highest in the first 3 years. yfinance gave XNAS a 2026-09 inception against the true 2021-01-21.

pillars.name: Issuer scale and closure record (record)
pillars.definition: Mean of the issuer's European ETF AUM (log) and its UCITS closures and mergers over 5 years per average line count. Weight 0 until a closure list is verified.
pillars.data_source: justETF closure lists (404); issuer annual reports; Investegate RNS titles (mostly NAV notices)
pillars.evidence: Small issuers prune ranges more often, but data test 9 found no working closed-fund list.

pillars.name: Switch-ready substitutes
pillars.definition: Number of other eligible LSE USD lines on the same or an approved equivalent index with TER within 0.10% and CST10 within 15 bps of this line; a different issuer counts double. A substitute counts only if it passes ELG08. 0 scores worst and 2 or more saturates.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv after the pending edits (add EXUS, ACWD, SPYY; remove EQAC and duplicates), with gates applied; CST01, CST10 | STATUS: verified for iShares-only sleeves; unverified and fails closed for Vanguard, Invesco and Xtrackers lines until ter_history is seeded from another source (justETF snapshots from now on, or annual reports via the Central Bank of Ireland register)
pillars.evidence: VWRA has FWRA, plus ACWD and SPYY as approved equivalents once added and owner-checked; the S&P 500 lines substitute for each other; XNAS has CNDX and EQQU. EXUS has none.

pillars.name: Counterparty and lending exposure (record)
pillars.definition: Physical fund: average % of NAV on loan over 1 year. Swap fund: replication and counterparties as a flag, plus net swap exposure % when available. Weight 0 until swap exposure percentages are verified.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK lending table (verified); justETF profile counterparties (verified); Invesco 406; Xtrackers JS app
pillars.evidence: UCITS caps counterparty exposure at 10% of NAV with collateral. Data test 10: swap exposure percentages cannot be fetched.

pillars.name: Benchmark-change history (record)
pillars.definition: Number of benchmark or provider changes, built from the weekly snapshot of the benchmark field from the first real snapshot onward, plus 1 for a pending consultation flagged by EVT04. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: Weekly snapshot store (not started; writer in the files to create); EVT04 output; current KID only
pillars.evidence: Issuers switch indices to cut licence fees (Vanguard 2012). Issuers publish only the latest KID, and no snapshot store exists yet (data tests 8, 11).

pillars.name: CAPE yield and CAPE against own history (record)
pillars.definition: Records US 1/CAPE and the US CAPE z-score against its 20-year history weekly. Regional 1/CAPE is recorded once config/cape.csv rows pass EVT10's code check. Weight 0, and missing for every exposure in scoring. The US-only series can be rebuilt in REC04 as a pre-registered variant (N_TRIALS + 1).
pillars.data_source: Shiller ie_data.xls: link scraped from shillerdata.com each run, with the last good img1.wsimg.com link cached as a fallback when the site resets (data test 12). Dates are read as strings and the month is derived from row order ((year-1871) x 12 + month rows). The stale Yale file is never used. Regional CAPE is unverified.
pillars.evidence: CAPE predicts 10-15 year returns (Campbell and Shiller 1998), but the 10-year R2 comes from overlapping windows (Boudoukh, Richardson and Whitelaw 2008). The US leg is verified (to 2026.10, CAPE 40.71); the regional leg is not.

pillars.name: Beta-consistent expected excess return in % a year (FIT04 input)
pillars.definition:
For equity exposures:
E[R_i - R_f] = beta_i x ERP_world + clip(sum_j b_j x (x_ij - x_VWRA,j), -2%, +2%) - (CST10_i - CST10_VWRA)/100.
- beta_i is the single FAC05 beta (univariate, 120 months, Ledoit-Wolf, on the ELG07 world reference). The same number is used in FIT04, RSK01 and RSK04. ERP_world = 4.0%.
- b_j are unestimated priors, labelled as such in every weekly output. EXR06: +0.5% per unit of REER z. EXR08: -0.01% per point of relative return. FAC01: +1.5% per unit of beta. FAC02: +1.5%. FAC03 (CMA orthogonalised to HML): +1.0%. FAC04: +1.0%. Because CMA is orthogonalised, value is not paid twice.
- REC04 also runs a pre-registered variant with all b_j = 0 (pure beta x ERP minus cost). This shows whether the priors or the data drive qualification.
Gold: beta x ERP plus an EXR11 percentile table (below 25th +1%, 25-50 +0.5%, 50-75 0%, above 75 -1%). Bonds: EXR10 minus the 3-month T-bill. Gold and bond values are context only.
The constants live in config/pillar_scales.yaml (to be created) under the frozen config hash. Weight 0 (derived).
Built-in check: with all tilts at 0 and equal costs, FIT04 = 0 for every equity exposure. With the single beta this holds identically, and the tolerance stays ±0.1%.
pillars.data_source: EXR06, EXR08, FAC01-FAC05, CST10 (verified); EXR10 (unverified, context), EXR11 (verified); 3-month T-bill from FRED DTB3 via curl --http1.1 (verified to 2026-11-05), fallback the cached last good value with an age flag
pillars.evidence: CAPM-consistent pricing (Sharpe 1964) makes alpha equal tilt minus cost. Round 3 (quant, blocking): EXR02's 60-month multifactor beta and FIT04's 120-month univariate beta differed (QQQ vs VT 1.239 vs 1.124), giving +0.46% a year of phantom alpha that acts as backdoor momentum. Fixed by using one beta.

pillars.name: Multi-ratio valuation yield (context)
pillars.definition: Mean robust z-score, against VWRA, of holdings' E/P, B/P, CF/P and S/P (yfinance returns these as yields under P/E labels; documented). Weight 0. Shown weekly and logged in REC02. It has no history for REC04, so it is context.
pillars.data_source: yfinance funds_data equity_holdings (verified, e.g. VWRA.L 'Price/Earnings' 0.0489 = 4.89% E/P); iShares P/E and P/B fields
pillars.evidence: Value predicts across countries (Asness, Moskowitz and Pedersen 2013), but cheap regions trailed VT in both 2015-19 and 2020-26.

pillars.name: Dividend yield after withholding (record)
pillars.definition: Dividends of the same-index US proxy with ex-dates in the 12 months ending today, divided by price, after fund-level withholding, in %. Accumulating UCITS lines report 0, hence the proxy. No buyback leg. INDA is flagged (no dividend in 23 months). Weight 0. It can be rebuilt in REC04 from proxy dividend history as a pre-registered variant.
pillars.data_source: yfinance Ticker.dividends of the proxy, window anchored to today (verified, e.g. VT 1.56%); TAX01
pillars.evidence: Payout yield predicts returns (Boudoukh et al. 2007), but S&P DJI buyback data returns 403.

pillars.name: CMA consensus 10-year return (context)
pillars.definition: Mean 10-year nominal USD expected return across at least 3 houses, shrunk toward VWRA's by 1 / (1 + range / 2 points). Rows in config/cma.csv (to be created) carry house, exposure, horizon, nominal_usd, url, quoted_text and published_on. Code confirms each number and rejects rows older than 200 days. Weight 0; a cross-check on EXR02 only.
pillars.data_source: config/cma.csv, filled by EVT10 (file does not exist yet)
pillars.evidence: Combining forecasts reduces error (Clemen 1989), but house CMAs are largely CAPE-built, so scoring them would count value again.

pillars.name: Currency valuation
pillars.definition:
Exposure-weighted z-score of each non-USD currency's BIS real effective exchange rate (broad basket) against its expanding mean, needing at least 10 years of data, inverted so cheaper scores higher. Release-lagged.
Coverage rule: missing for an exposure unless REER covers at least 70% of its non-USD weight. Before 10 years of data exist (about 2004-01), it is missing for every exposure.
Currencies: every currency above 2% of any sleeve's weight, including TWD and KRW (EIMI is about 26% Taiwan and 18% Korea).
Currency weights: live from holdings. In REC04 they come from the ELG07 frozen region mix with its stated as-of date (earliest documented index weights), plus a disclosed sensitivity run on today's mix. BIS files are revised vintages, not point-in-time; this is disclosed.
Weight 0.4 of EXR (8% of X), inside the value-cluster cap.
pillars.data_source: Primary: BIS WS_EER M.R.B.<cc> CSV (verified 2026-11-07: XM and TW to 2026-09; KR from 1994-01). Backup: FRED RB<cc>BIS via curl --http1.1 (RBXMBIS, RBJPBIS, RBGBBIS, RBCNBIS, RBINBIS, RBTWBIS, RBKRBIS; verified 1994-01 to 2026-07). Then the cached last good value with an age flag. Holdings currency weights.
pillars.evidence: Real exchange rates revert with a 3-5 year half-life (Rogoff 1996), and currency value predicts currency returns (Menkhoff et al. 2017). This matters for an unhedged owner whose AED is pegged to the USD. Round 3: FRED was unreachable in data test 14, and Taiwan and Korea were missing.

pillars.name: Currency carry (record)
pillars.definition: Sum over non-USD currencies of unhedged weight x (local short rate - US short rate), in %, point-in-time. Computed only if rates of age 60 days or less cover at least 70% of the exposure's non-USD weight, from one consistent source. Otherwise it is missing for every exposure, VWRA included. Weight 0 and not an EXR02 input.
pillars.data_source: Candidates: BIS WS_CBPOL policy rates (EUR, GBP, INR, JPY, CNY, KRW to 2026-09/10; no Taiwan series); ECB data-api €STR (verified 2.442 on 2026-11-05); BoE IADB SONIA IUDSOIA (verified 3.7335 on 2026-11-04); Bank of Canada Valet. OECD 3-month EUR and GBP series end 2026-01.
pillars.evidence: Carry earns a premium (Lustig, Roussanov and Verdelhan 2011), but it is a 1-3 month premium that crashes in risk-off episodes (Brunnermeier, Nagel and Pedersen 2008). That is a poor fit for 15-year quarterly targets.

pillars.name: Long-term reversal
pillars.definition: USD total return of the sleeve's reference index (spliced under ELG07, ^NDX before QQQ) from month -60 to month -13, minus the world reference's over the same window. Price-based, so it is rebuilt exactly in REC04. Weight 0.6 of EXR (12% of X). EXR06 + EXR08 + FAC01 are capped at 25% of X.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy adjusted closes; ^NDX (verified from 1985-10); Ken French market returns for spliced history
pillars.evidence: Country indices mean-revert over 3-5 years (Richards 1997; Balvers, Wu and Gilliland 2000). It is weak after 2000, hence the cap. Its rho with EXR06 and FAC01 is checked before launch (REC03).

pillars.name: Index construction drag (record)
pillars.definition: Index one-way turnover x asset-class trading cost, plus a front-running estimate for indices with predictable additions, in bps a year. Turnover comes from 12 months of iShares holdings snapshots. Weight 0 until turnover exists for every sleeve's index.
pillars.data_source: iShares holdings snapshots (not started; snapshot writer in the files to create; single latest-holdings.csv verified); Petajisto (2011) parameters; yfinance annualHoldingsTurnover (None)
pillars.evidence: Index-change costs are about 21-28 bps a year for the S&P 500 and 38-77 bps for the Russell 2000 (Petajisto 2011). Data test 15 found no snapshot store, so the earlier 'building from 2026-11' label was corrected.

pillars.name: Bond expected return (diversifier sleeve, context)
pillars.definition: Yield to worst minus expected default loss by rating (AAA-A 0.05%, BBB 0.2%, BB 1%, B and below 3%, x 0.6), minus TER, plus Treasury roll-down at the fund's duration, plus hedge carry for a hedged class, in %. Ranks bond lines within the diversifier sleeve and informs the owner's choice of D. Never sets a target.
pillars.data_source: iShares UK bond holdings CSV (verified, but it has no yield-to-worst or rating columns); iShares bond product-page weighted YTM and credit-rating fields (to be probed); Treasury curve from FRED DGS1-DGS30 via curl --http1.1, with cached fallback
pillars.evidence: Starting yield explains most of a bond fund's 5-10 year return (Leibowitz, Bova and Kogelman 2014). Round 3 (data): the CSV lacks yield and rating, so the status was corrected until the product-page probe passes. Context only, so there is no weight impact.

pillars.name: Gold real-price valuation (gold sleeve, context)
pillars.definition: Percentile of the monthly USD gold price deflated by US CPI within its history from 1975-01 to the latest month (release-lagged). Feeds EXR02's gold table and the owner note for the gold 0-or-5% decision. Never sets a target.
pillars.data_source: World Bank Pink Sheet CMO-Historical-Data-Monthly.xlsx, 'Monthly Prices' sheet, header row 4, Gold column, 1960M01 to 2026M10 (verified; scrape the GUID link each run, cache the last good file); FRED CPIAUCSL via curl --http1.1 (verified to 2026-09), fallback the cached value with an age flag
pillars.evidence: A high real gold price has been followed by low real returns (Erb and Harvey 2013).

pillars.name: Country risk premium (record)
pillars.definition: Look-through weighted Damodaran country risk premium, in %. Weight 0. It can be rebuilt in REC04 from Damodaran's annual archives as a pre-registered variant.
pillars.data_source: Damodaran ctryprem.xlsx (download verified)
pillars.evidence: Country ratings explain returns in sample (Erb, Harvey and Viskanta 1996), but out-of-sample evidence is weak.

pillars.name: Value loading (common factor set)
pillars.definition: HML beta from a 60-month Newey-West regression of the reference index's USD excess return on one common factor set: Ken French Developed Mkt-RF, SMB, HML, RMW, CMA_perp and Developed WML. This set is used for every equity sleeve (S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, EXUS, EIMI) and for VWRA. EIMI's regression on Developed factors is a disclosed approximation, with a REC04 sensitivity run on the Emerging set. Estimated monthly using only data released by then (1-month lag; Ken French files are revised vintages, disclosed), shrunk by min(1, |t| / 2) and scored as the loading minus VWRA's loading on the same set. Weight 0.12 of FAC (4.8% of X), inside the value-cluster cap.
pillars.data_source: Ken French Developed 5 factors and Developed momentum files (verified, 1990-07 to 2026-09); yfinance monthly returns and ELG07 splices
pillars.evidence: Fama and French (1992, 1998, 2015). The premium was weak from about 2007 to 2020 (Fama and French 2021), so its weight is small. Round 3 (quant, skeptic, data; blocking): loadings from different regional factor sets were not comparable, and Ken French publishes no ACWI set.

pillars.name: Profitability loading (common factor set)
pillars.definition: RMW beta from the same common-set point-in-time regression, shrunk by min(1, |t| / 2), scored as the loading minus VWRA's on the same set. Weight 0.30 of FAC.
pillars.data_source: Ken French Developed 5 factors and momentum (verified); yfinance
pillars.evidence: Novy-Marx (2013); Fama and French (2015, 2017); Asness, Frazzini and Pedersen (2019). Robust across regions.

pillars.name: Investment loading, orthogonalised to value
pillars.definition: Loading on CMA_perp, the residual of Developed CMA regressed on Developed HML over an expanding window ending at the decision date (point-in-time). Taken from the same common-set regression, shrunk by min(1, |t| / 2), relative to VWRA's. Weight 0.28 of FAC. Because CMA is orthogonalised, FAC03 measures investment exposure beyond value and sits outside the value-cluster cap. FAC01 vs FAC03 is a mandatory REC03 pair with a 0.7 threshold.
pillars.data_source: Ken French Developed 5 factors (verified); yfinance
pillars.evidence: Fama and French (2015) found HML largely redundant given CMA, so raw CMA would carry value exposure. Round 3 (quant): effective value weight was about 36% of X; orthogonalising restores the 25% cap.

pillars.name: Size loading, conditional on quality
pillars.definition: The SMB beta from the common-set regression counts only if the RMW beta is 0 or above; otherwise 0. Relative to VWRA's. Weight 0.30 of FAC.
pillars.data_source: Ken French Developed 5 factors (verified); yfinance
pillars.evidence: The plain size premium is weak (Alquist, Israel and Moskowitz 2018) but appears once junk is controlled for (Asness et al. 2018).

pillars.name: Single market beta (univariate) and residual alpha (context)
pillars.definition: The system's one beta: from a separate univariate regression, not the factor regression, of the sleeve reference index's monthly USD excess return on the ELG07 world reference excess return over 120 months, Ledoit-Wolf shrunk and release-lagged. It is used for EXR02 (beta x ERP), FIT04 (beta_i,P = beta_i / beta_P), RSK01's stress part, RSK04 and RSK07. The annualised intercept and its t-statistic from the common-set factor regression are shown as context. Weight 0. Unit test: VWRA's loadings minus VWRA's loadings = 0 on every factor.
pillars.data_source: yfinance and ELG07 splices; Ken French market + RF for the world reference before VT
pillars.evidence: Round 3 (quant, blocking): the earlier 'world beta from the same regression' did not exist, because that regression used a regional market factor. Rewarding low beta would favour defensive funds; EXR02 prices beta explicitly. Past alpha does not persist (Carhart 1997).

pillars.name: Excess drawdown path (merged)
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns; ^NDX (verified); Ken French market series for splices; world reference per ELG07
pillars.evidence: Nasdaq-100 fell about 80% in 2000-02 against about 50% for the world. Round 3 (quant): holdability is about the actual loss, and beta-scaling excused a 1.2-beta sleeve's 60% drawdown.

pillars.name: Excess time under water (RSK01 component)
pillars.definition: Longest peak-to-recovery spell in months minus the world's over the same expanding window; an unrecovered drawdown counts to date. Weight 0 on its own: it enters X only through RSK01. Logged separately for REC03.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns; ^NDX splice
pillars.evidence: Japan took about 34 years and Nasdaq-100 about 15 years to regain their peaks. Long recoveries make owners abandon a plan.

pillars.name: Downside-upside beta asymmetry (one-sided)
pillars.definition: Beta to the world reference in down months minus beta in up months over 120 months, point-in-time. One-sided against VWRA: only asymmetry above VWRA's is penalised, with k = 0.2, and lower asymmetry earns nothing above 50. Weight 0.35 of RSK.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Downside beta is priced (Ang, Chen and Xing 2006). Correlations rise in falling markets (Longin and Solnik 2001). Its overlap with RSK01 and RSK05 is a mandatory REC03 pair.

pillars.name: Stress-window shortfall, point-in-time (RSK01 component)
pillars.definition: Mean of (exposure return - beta x world return) over every listed stress window that ended at least 1 month before date t, with beta from FAC05. The windows are Oct 2007-Mar 2009, Feb-Mar 2020 and calendar 2022. If no window has ended, the pillar is missing for all exposures, VWRA included. Only shortfalls count. Weight 0 on its own; it enters through RSK01. Unit test: a REC04 run dated 2015-01 sees only the 2007-09 window.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy history; world reference per ELG07
pillars.evidence: Round 2 (quant): fixed windows used before they happened were a look-ahead that would flatter REC04.

pillars.name: Tail fatness (one-sided)
pillars.definition: Monthly 95% CVaR divided by monthly volatility over 120 months. Scale-free. One-sided against VWRA: only fatter tails than VWRA's are penalised, with k = 0.5. Weight 0.30 of RSK.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Tail risk beyond the normal is a holdability hazard (Kelly and Jiang 2014). Negative coskewness may be priced (Harvey and Siddique 2000).

pillars.name: Portfolio drawdown budget (constraint)
pillars.definition: Replays the proposed target mix through every listed stress window (2008-09, 2011, 2020 Q1, 2022) that ended at least 1 month before the decision date, monthly and spliced. Worst loss minus the world's worst must be 5 points or less, and tilts are scaled down until it holds. Weight 0. Unit test: a 2015-01 run sees only 2008-09 and 2011.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns; target mix; world reference per ELG07
pillars.evidence: GOAL success measure: worst drawdown against the world market.

pillars.name: Risk-contribution ratio (constraint)
pillars.definition: Each sleeve's share of portfolio variance (120-month Ledoit-Wolf monthly covariance) divided by its capital weight; must be 1.5 or less at target weights. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns; target mix
pillars.evidence: Capital weights understate a volatile satellite's risk (Qian 2005; Maillard, Roncalli and Teiletche 2010).

pillars.name: Drawdown protocol, volatility and regret display (context)
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L closes; owner positions (core-only fallback)
pillars.evidence: Investors lose 1-1.7 points a year trading around drawdowns (Dichev 2007; Morningstar 'Mind the Gap').

pillars.name: Breadth of holdings (context)
pillars.definition: Effective number of issuers: 1 / sum of squared look-through issuer weights, with share classes merged, log-scaled and saturating at 500. Weight 0. Shown weekly.
pillars.data_source: iShares latest-holdings.csv by productId; for VWRA and FWRA, the SSAC holdings stand-in (ELG07, constraint-only, verified 2026-11-07)
pillars.evidence: About 4% of US stocks created all net wealth (Bessembinder 2018).

pillars.name: Country and currency mix (context)
pillars.definition: Largest country weight, half the sum of |country weight - world weight|, non-USD share and a hedged flag. Weight 0; portfolio limits sit in FIT07.
pillars.data_source: Holdings Location and Market Currency columns (iShares CSV; Vanguard month-end region weights for VWRA; ELG07 stand-ins)
pillars.evidence: Scoring this at fund level would penalise an S&P 500 sleeve twice.

pillars.name: Sector mix and index concentration (context)
pillars.definition: Half the sum of |GICS sector weight - world sector weight|, the top-10 weight, and its percentile in the index's own logged history (from the snapshot store once it exists). Weight 0; portfolio limits sit in FIT08 and FIT09.
pillars.data_source: Holdings Sector column; SSAC as the world sector reference and VWRA stand-in (IT + Communication 35.95% on 05/Nov/2026); weekly holdings snapshots (not started)
pillars.evidence: Evidence that concentration predicts returns is mixed, so it is shown as something to watch. The history percentile reads missing until the snapshot store has data.

pillars.name: Restricted-market exposure (gate only)
pillars.definition: Look-through weight in markets listed in config/restricted_markets.csv (to be created). Every row carries a primary-source citation and date, added by EVT07 and checked by code. Above 5%, the line cannot receive deposits. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: Holdings Location column (verified); config/restricted_markets.csv
pillars.evidence: Russia 2022: removal at an effectively zero price and suspended ETFs. The hazard is counted once.

pillars.name: Specialised or thematic hype (line gate)
pillars.definition: Flag 1 for a narrow thematic, single-industry or single-frontier-country fund launched within 5 years or after a top-quintile 36-month index return. Flag 0.5 for other narrow sector or theme funds. Flag 0 for broad funds. A flag of 1 blocks deposits; 0.5 is shown as a warning. The inflow clause starts only once DUR03 has 52 weeks of real snapshots. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv scope tags and first_date; yfinance index history
pillars.evidence: Specialised ETFs launched into hype underperform by about 6% a year over 5 years (Ben-David, Franzoni, Kim and Moussawi 2023).

pillars.name: Sleeve gap (routing input)
pillars.definition: For each sleeve: gap = target x (portfolio value + C) - sleeve value, in US$. Weight 0. If positions are missing or older than 35 days, the whole deposit goes to the core.
pillars.data_source: config/portfolio.yaml positions [{line, units, avg_cost_usd, as_of}] (block not yet added); later the IBKR statement parser (inputs/ibkr/, not yet created); yfinance .L prices
pillars.evidence: Rebalancing with new cash keeps the mix on target without selling (Jaconetti, Kinniry and Zilbering 2010).

pillars.name: Months to cure drift with deposits
pillars.definition: For each overweight sleeve: (sleeve value - band max x portfolio value) / monthly deposit, plus the number of consecutive month-ends outside its band. Weight 0; used by S3.
pillars.data_source: Engine, from FIT01 history and positions (unbuilt)
pillars.evidence: Separates drift that deposits will fix from a breach only a sale can fix.

pillars.name: Overlap with current holdings (context)
pillars.definition: Sum over securities of min(fund weight, portfolio look-through weight), in %. Weight 0, shown to the owner.
pillars.data_source: iShares holdings CSV; ELG07 constraint-only stand-ins (SSAC for VWRA and FWRA, CSPX for VUAA and SPXS, CNDX for XNAS, SWDA ex-US for EXUS); portfolio = core if positions are missing
pillars.evidence: A VUAA or SPXS deposit mostly re-buys VWRA's 62% US. Active share does not predict returns (Frazzini, Friedman and Pomorski 2016), so this is context.

pillars.name: Expected alpha against the current portfolio (equity sleeves)
pillars.definition:
alpha_i = E[R_i - R_f] - beta_i,P x E[R_P - R_f], in % a year. E comes from EXR02, and E[R_P - R_f] = sum of w_k x EXR02_k.
beta_i,P = beta_i / beta_P, where beta_i is the FAC05 beta and beta_P = sum of w_k x beta_k (single-index model, one beta source). P is the core alone until positions exist.
With zero tilts and equal costs, alpha_i = beta_i x ERP - (beta_i / beta_P) x beta_P x ERP = 0 identically.
Applies to equity sleeves only, at 40% of their FIT view; for gold and bond sleeves it is context. It must be above 0 for a score-driven target (only after REC04 passes) and is shown as a warning on owner policy targets.
pillars.data_source: EXR02; FAC05; owner positions (core-only fallback)
pillars.evidence: An asset raises the Sharpe ratio when its expected excess return exceeds beta x the portfolio's (Treynor and Black 1973). Round 3 (quant, blocking): the beta mismatch gave the Nasdaq-100 +0.46% a year of phantom alpha; one beta removes it.

pillars.name: Down-market correlation with the portfolio
pillars.definition: Correlation of monthly returns with the current portfolio (core if positions are missing) in months when the world fell, over 120 months with at least 20 such months.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Correlations rise in falling markets (Longin and Solnik 2001). Scale-free. It shares a covariance with FIT06 and FIT10, so the three are a mandatory REC03 triple; any pair with |rho| of 0.85 or more is merged before launch.

pillars.name: Diversification return
pillars.definition: Change in 0.5 x (sum w_i sigma_i^2 - sigma_p^2), annualised in bps, moving from the current mix to 95% current + 5% this fund (120-month monthly).
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Booth and Fama (1992); Willenbrock (2011). Rewards volatile, low-correlation assets, which offsets any low-volatility bias.

pillars.name: US look-through weight (constraint)
pillars.definition: Portfolio US weight after the order and at target, minus the world US weight. Hard limit +10 points. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: Holdings Location (iShares CSV; Vanguard month-end region weights for VWRA; SWDA ex-US for EXUS)
pillars.evidence: VWRA is already about 62% US.

pillars.name: Sector deviation and tech share (constraint)
pillars.definition: Information Technology plus Communication Services at no more than world + 10 points, and total sector deviation at no more than 15 points, after the order and at target. Weight 0. Fails open for the core and closed for satellites if sector data is missing or the stand-in is unreconciled (ELG10).
pillars.data_source: Holdings Sector column; SSAC as world reference and VWRA stand-in, cross-checked against yfinance VT sector weightings (ELG10)
pillars.evidence: The largest concentrated drawdowns came from sector bubbles (2000-02). Nasdaq-100 is over 50% technology.

pillars.name: Single-name concentration (constraint)
pillars.definition: Largest single-company look-through weight, share classes combined, 7% or less after the order and at target. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: iShares holdings CSV; SSAC stand-in for VWRA (AAPL 5.10%, NVDA 4.21% on 05/Nov/2026); CSPX and CNDX stand-ins
pillars.evidence: Single-name risk is not compensated (Bessembinder 2018). Stacking S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 on VWRA multiplies the same mega-caps.

pillars.name: Ex-ante tracking error against VWRA
pillars.definition: Forecast annual tracking error of the post-order portfolio against VWRA (120-month Ledoit-Wolf), in %. One-sided, with no penalty up to 2%; hard limit 3%. The only scored active-risk measure.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns
pillars.evidence: The first success measure is money-weighted return against VWRA, so active risk is the budget every tilt spends (Grinold and Kahn).

pillars.name: Line count and duplicate-exposure guard (gate)
pillars.definition: Blocks a candidate whose 3-year weekly correlation with a held line is 0.97 or more on the same index family, unless it is that line's designated replacement under S1, S2 or allocation step 3(d). At most 4 lines in total, counting diversifier lines and frozen old lines. A replacement that would make a fifth line is not allowed. Positions under 2% are flagged. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: config/portfolio.yaml positions (core-only fallback); yfinance weekly returns; universe index families
pillars.evidence: GOAL: a few hours a month and one or two funds per buy.

pillars.name: 12-1 momentum against VWRA (record)
pillars.definition: USD return from month -12 to -1 of the reference index minus the world reference's. Weight 0; logged by REC02 and tested in REC04 as one pre-registered variant.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy adjusted closes
pillars.evidence: Momentum decayed after publication (McLean and Pontiff 2016), and S3 here lost 4-6% a year in 2015-19.

pillars.name: Residual momentum against the world (record)
pillars.definition: Cumulative residual return over months -12 to -2 from a 36-month regression on world returns. Weight 0; tested in the REC04 momentum variant.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L and proxy monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Residual momentum has about half the crash risk (Blitz, Huij and Martens 2011), but it has MOM01's horizon problem.

pillars.name: Momentum-crash state (context)
pillars.definition: On when the world's 24-month return is below 0 and its 1-month return is above 0. Neutralises the recorded MOM01 and MOM02 values.
pillars.data_source: yfinance VWRA.L spliced with VT
pillars.evidence: Momentum crashes cluster in rebounds after bear markets (Daniel and Moskowitz 2016).

pillars.name: Core trend flag
pillars.definition: VWRA.L month-end close against its 10-month average, and the sign of its 12-1 return. Information only.
pillars.data_source: yfinance VWRA.L
pillars.evidence: Selling the core on trend (S8) trailed holding by 1-3 points a year.

pillars.name: Holdings and candidates against VWRA (weekly display)
pillars.definition: Excess USD return over VWRA.L for each holding and each sleeve's reference line over 1, 3 and 12 months, plus the 3-year information ratio. Display only; this is the weekly 'how is each holding doing' answer.
pillars.data_source: yfinance .L closes
pillars.evidence: Past relative performance persists only weakly (Carhart 1997), so it is shown, not scored.

pillars.name: Money-weighted return against a VWRA-only portfolio
pillars.definition: Since start and over rolling 12 months: the actual portfolio's money-weighted return after all costs, against a shadow VWRA-only portfolio with identical deposits. Also the money-weighted minus time-weighted gap, and worst drawdown against the world.
pillars.data_source: IBKR statements in inputs/ibkr/ (folder and parser to build); yfinance VWRA.L
pillars.evidence: GOAL success measure 1.

pillars.name: Point-in-time pick and pillar snapshot
pillars.data_source: Engine plan log and snapshot store (not yet created); yfinance .L closes; FRED via curl --http1.1 with ECB/BoE fallbacks and cached values
pillars.evidence: The live record is the only test of pillars without history. Data tests 19 and 21: the plan log does not exist yet.

pillars.name: Redundancy matrix and live information coefficient by exposure
pillars.definition:
Before launch, two redundancy checks:
- Exposure pillars, on the point-in-time panel REC04 reconstructs (sleeves x months, 2003-2026): the time-series average of monthly cross-sectional Spearman correlations (Fama-MacBeth style), with a block-bootstrap confidence interval using blocks of at least 24 months, reporting the effective number of sleeves. A pair whose |rho| is 0.85 or more at the lower confidence bound is merged. Mandatory pairs: EXR06/EXR08, EXR08/FAC01, FAC01/FAC03 (each must be below 0.7, or the lower-weighted pillar becomes record-only), RSK01/RSK03, RSK01/RSK05, RSK03/RSK05, FIT05/FIT06, FIT05/FIT10, FIT06/FIT10.
- Line pillars, the same test across lines within sleeves. Mandatory pairs: DUR01/CST06, CST03/CST04, CST02/TAX03.
Live: rank IC of each family and each record pillar against forward 13, 52 and 156-week returns versus VWRA, one row per exposure, with non-overlapping windows or Newey-West errors.
Low power is admitted (about 8 exposures, 4-5 effective clusters). So the main promotion route is reconstruction in REC04 as a pre-registered variant (N_TRIALS + 1). Live IC above 0 with t above 2 after 36 months is the secondary route. Demotion happens only after 36 months.
pillars.data_source: REC04 panel; engine score history from 2026-W45; yfinance .L closes
pillars.evidence: Round 3 (quant): a pooled sleeves x months Spearman overstated n because the 60/120-month values are heavily autocorrelated. Not yet run; it must be run before launch.

pillars.name: Exact-rule backtest and score-target gate
pillars.definition:
src/backtest.py re-runs the exact live exposure rule monthly: the X pillars and weights under the frozen config hash; X smoothed as the mean of the last 3 month-end values (the same definition live and in the backtest); the clip((X-55)/15) target, hysteresis, the satellite limits and the constraints.
Settings:
- MONTHLY = 681, the US$2 FX minimum, the US$1.70 commission, k-month batching per allocation 3(a), whole shares and the rolling-12 flow cap;
- both execution timings;
- expanding windows with Ken French and FRED release lags (revised vintages, disclosed), point-in-time stress windows, the single ELG07 world reference, the ^NDX splice and the dated frozen region mixes.
Periods: 2003-2014 (holdout; primary out-of-sample for EXUS and EIMI only, because REC07 already viewed it for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100), 2015-19, 2020-26 and full. A per-sleeve availability table sets each sleeve's start (series start + 60 months for FAC and EXR08, + 120 months for RSK). Sleeves without a passing splice are excluded and named.
Gate: a positive money-weighted excess over the world in every period under both timings, AND a deflated Sharpe probability above 0.95 computed on the monthly active return (strategy minus world reference, i.e. an information ratio), at N_TRIALS of 26 or more. The 26 are: 8 existing strategies, 4 design tilts, 4 REC04 variants, 5 REC07 mixes, 3 audit-round revisions informed by the 2015-2026 backtest, the b_j = 0 variant and the EIMI Emerging-factor sensitivity run; add 1 per further variant. dsr() in src/backtest.py must be patched to accept an excess-return series.
Until the gate passes, X sets no targets.
pillars.data_source: Engine; Ken French; BIS/FRED with fallbacks; yfinance; runs/backtest_latest.json (current file uses MONTHLY = 2500 and absolute Sharpe; to be re-run)
pillars.evidence: GOAL evidence rule. Round 3 (skeptic, blocking): dsr() took each strategy's absolute Sharpe, and the S0 world benchmark itself scored only 0.855, so any rule that is 85% or more VWRA could never pass whatever its merit. Testing active return measures the tilt itself.

pillars.name: Execution and funding log
pillars.data_source: IBKR statements and bank advice in inputs/ibkr/ (not yet created); funding block in config/portfolio.yaml (to be added); yfinance .L closes
pillars.better_when: lower cost and no systematic drift
pillars.evidence: S5 flipped sign between execution timings, so timing choices must be logged. The US$2 FX minimum is 29 bps of US$680.

pillars.name: Behaviour, sell log and attribution
pillars.definition: Monthly: deposits on schedule, days from deposit to order, every sale with its rule and hold counterfactual, and a Brinson split of active return against VWRA into owner-policy sleeve choice, score-driven sleeve choice and line choice. Also line regret 12 months after each buy against the best same-index line.
pillars.data_source: IBKR statements; runs/plan_log.csv; yfinance .L closes
pillars.better_when: all deposits on schedule; zero non-structural sells; line regret near or above 0
pillars.evidence: GOAL success measure: no unforced sells. The attribution shows which part adds or loses money.

pillars.name: Owner policy-mix test with exact live routing
pillars.data_source: yfinance VT, SPY, QQQ, EFA, EEM, EWC monthly adjusted closes (verified); ^NDX splice; Ken French market series for the ELG07 world reference before VT
pillars.better_when: higher, and positive in every period
pillars.evidence: Preliminary scratchpad run (not to definition, US$2,500 deposits): 80/10/10 vs world lost in 2003-07 (14.07% vs 14.94%) and won after 2008. That is a regime bet, so no policy currently passes. Round 3 (skeptic): at the real US$681 deposit the fixed-cost drag is about 3.7 times larger than at US$2,500.

pillars.name: Recession indicators
pillars.definition: 10-year minus 3-month spread (level, and months inverted in the last 24) and the real-time Sahm rule against 0.5, with false-alarm notes. Context. On a FRED outage the cached last good value is shown with its age.
pillars.data_source: FRED T10Y3M, SAHMREALTIME via curl --http1.1 (verified); cached-value fallback with age flag
pillars.evidence: They forecast recessions (Estrella and Mishkin 1998; Sahm 2019) but not returns out of sample (Welch and Goyal 2008).

pillars.name: Credit and financial stress
pillars.definition: US high-yield OAS and EM corporate OAS as a 3-year percentile and 3-month change (both short-history; FRED holds only a 3-year licence window). A long-history credit percentile comes from Moody's Baa minus 10-year (20-year percentile). Also the St. Louis Fed stress index, the Chicago NFCI, and EPU and GPR percentiles. Context for the drawdown note.
pillars.data_source: FRED BAA10Y (verified 2026-11-07: 1986-01 to 2026-11-05), BAMLH0A0HYM2 and BAMLEMCBPIOAS (from 2023-11-07 only), STLFSI4, NFCI, via curl --http1.1 with cached fallback; policyuncertainty.com; Caldara-Iacoviello GPR
pillars.evidence: Spreads carry stress information (Gilchrist and Zakrajsek 2012) but have no out-of-sample timing value. Round 3 (data): a 20-year OAS percentile could not be computed from a 3-year series.

pillars.name: Volatility regime (execution caution)
pillars.definition: VIX, VIX/VIX3M and MOVE. When VIX is above 30 or VIX/VIX3M is above 1, the execution ladder starts at mid instead of mid plus a quarter spread and avoids the first and last 30 minutes (allocation 3(g)). Never delays or skips the deposit.
pillars.data_source: yfinance ^VIX, ^VIX3M, ^MOVE
pillars.evidence: Spreads widen when volatility spikes (Chordia, Roll and Subrahmanyam 2001).

pillars.name: Rates, inflation, dollar and stock-bond regime
pillars.definition: 10-year TIPS yield, 5y5y breakeven, US CPI, 12-month broad-dollar change, AED/USD against 3.6725, 36-month equity-bond correlation and the US excess CAPE yield. Context for the owner's decision on the diversifier share D.
pillars.data_source: FRED DFII10, T5YIFR, CPIAUCSL, DTWEXBGS via curl --http1.1 (verified), with the cached last good value and age flag on outage; yfinance AED=X, VT, IEF, AGGU.L; Shiller via the shillerdata.com link with the cached-link fallback
pillars.evidence: The stock-bond correlation depends on the inflation regime (Ilmanen 2003).

pillars.name: Fund corporate actions
pillars.definition: Agent scans held and shortlisted lines for closure, merger, liquidation, share-class conversion, delisting, ISIN or ticker change, or loss of the USD line. Severity: 0 none, 1 watch, 2 review (confirmed notice), 3 act. Two dated, cited sources are required, and a primary source (an issuer notice, or an RNS item via Investegate with daily NAV notices filtered out) for severity 2 or more. Penalty-only in the line score (50, 40, 25, 0). Severity 2 or more blocks deposits and opens S1.
pillars.data_source: Web search; investegate.co.uk RNS pages (verified); issuer notices
pillars.evidence: DECISION_RULES rule 1 structural triggers. LSE RNS returns 403; Investegate works.

pillars.name: Fees, structure, KID and cheaper substitutes
pillars.definition: Agent detects and cites TER, replication, lending, distribution-policy and domicile changes, KID availability, new LSE USD lines and fee cuts on any sleeve's index. Confirmed TER changes go into CST01's ter_history. Severity: an adverse confirmed change is 2. The cheaper-substitute trigger is computed by code, not the agent: an incumbent gets severity 1 when an eligible substitute's CST10 is 10 bps or more lower. Penalty-only.
pillars.data_source: Web search; justETF profile pages (verified); issuer KIDs and notices; CST10 for the substitute test | STATUS: verified for iShares-only sleeves; unverified and fails closed for Vanguard, Invesco and Xtrackers lines until ter_history is seeded from another source (justETF snapshots from now on, or annual reports via the Central Bank of Ireland register)
pillars.evidence: A fee rise is a structural trigger, and redirecting new money to a cheaper line costs nothing (Sharpe 1991). Round 3 (portfolio): the substitute test was code-computable.

pillars.name: Satellite thesis log (record only)
pillars.definition: Quarterly, for each held or policy satellite, the agent records cited structural facts bearing on 10-year cash flows or investability, with base rates, and a verdict (intact, weakened or broken). Weight 0: it never changes a score or freezes a sleeve. Facts on the fixed list (sanctions, capital controls, exchange closure, delisting) go to EVT07.
pillars.data_source: Web search with at least 2 cited sources; central banks, regulators, statistics agencies
pillars.evidence: News sentiment is priced within days (Tetlock 2007). The log lets REC03 test whether verdicts predict anything.

pillars.name: Index methodology, reclassification and mega-cap events
pillars.definition: Agent tracks benchmark switches, provider consultations, capping-rule changes, special rebalances, country reclassifications and single-company events that move top-10 weights. Weight 0 in X. Feeds DUR08 and triggers an immediate recompute of FIT and CON from fresh holdings.
pillars.data_source: Web search; MSCI, FTSE Russell, S&P DJI and Nasdaq announcements; SEC EDGAR
pillars.evidence: Index rule changes shift the exposure before holdings files show it (Petajisto 2011).

pillars.name: Issuer, custodian and counterparty health
pillars.definition: Agent detects issuers exiting European ETFs, custodian or administrator changes (including ETC vault and custodian changes, which trigger a DUR02 re-check), lending or swap-counterparty incidents, and regulatory sanctions on an issuer or depositary. Applies to every line of that issuer. Penalty-only; severity 2 or more blocks deposits.
pillars.data_source: Web search; Central Bank of Ireland, CSSF and FCA notices; issuer releases
pillars.evidence: Issuer-level events hit every line at once and appear in fund data only late.

pillars.name: Tax and legal regime for the owner
pillars.data_source: Web search; IRS, Revenue.ie, UAE MoF, CRA
pillars.evidence: The Irish wrapper is worth 30-40 bps a year plus estate-tax protection, more than any tested edge.

pillars.name: Sanctions, capital controls and market access (gate)
pillars.definition: Agent detects sanctions, capital controls, exchange closures, investment bans and delisting risk affecting look-through holdings. It estimates the affected weight per line and proposes rows for config/restricted_markets.csv with a primary-source URL and quoted text, which code checks before CON04 uses them. Severity 3 freezes deposits to affected lines. Weight 0 in X.
pillars.data_source: Web search; OFAC, EU and UK sanctions lists; index-provider notices
pillars.evidence: Russia 2022 losses could not be traded around. Counted once, as a gate.

pillars.name: Broker, venue and funding channel
pillars.definition: Agent watches IBKR changes for UAE clients (US$1.70 minimum, FX terms and US$2 minimum, product access including ETC classification, KID), fractional LSE ETF shares, LSE outages, the CBUAE peg stance and UAE remittance and USD-wire fees. Weight 0. Confirmed changes update the allocator constants and the funding block.
pillars.data_source: Web search; IBKR pricing and notices; LSE notices; CBUAE releases
pillars.evidence: Ticket and FX minimums and whole-share buying drive the monthly split and line choice. Fractional shares would reopen CSPX and CNDX.

pillars.name: Deposit-week calendar and market dislocations
pillars.definition: Agent lists deposit-week events (FOMC, US CPI and payrolls, ECB, BoE and BoJ, index rebalance days, US and UK holidays) and any ETF dislocation or LSE outage, and recommends the order day and hour. It may delay an order by at most 1 week, and every delay and its reason is logged in REC05. It never skips a deposit or triggers a sale. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: Web search; central-bank, index-provider and exchange calendars
pillars.evidence: Spreads widen around releases and rebalances (Petajisto 2011, 2017). The S5 backtest showed execution timing can flip results, so the choice is logged.

pillars.name: CMA and valuation data harvest (code-checked)
pillars.definition: Each quarter the agent extracts numbers only, from CMA releases and regional CAPE readings. Each row goes to config/cma.csv or config/cape.csv with a URL, the quoted text span and a date. Code fetches the page and confirms the number appears in the span; failing rows are marked unverified and never read. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: Web search; house PDFs; StarCapital and Research Affiliates pages
pillars.evidence: Only record or context pillars (EXR01, EXR05) read these files.

allocation_method:
Three layers. The pool and its limits are policy. Targets come from owner policy that has passed REC07, or from scores after REC04 passes. Routing happens monthly; the weekly run never moves money.

1. THE POOL. Sleeve lines were verified on yfinance as USD LSE lines on 2026-11-07.
